messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT 5601234567 - High p99 tail latency observed for streaming endpoints in us-west-2. Metric spike detected: p99 > 1.2s, error rate +2%. Auto-snooze: 5m. @oncall-mike paged.

mike: acked. jumping in. grabbing dashboards and recent deploys. any obvious rolls?

sara: no deploys in last 30m from runtime. seeing large increase in KV eviction rate on pool-kv-17, slab usage trending to 98%.

ashley: confirmed from SRE dashboards: eviction/sec jumped x5 at 2026-03-15T10:42Z. streaming tail stalls correlate with eviction bursts. p95 ~ 220ms, p99 ~ 1.25s.

mike: ok — scope: streaming generation endpoints (streaming=true), primarily model variants gptx-small-01 and gptx-small-01-quant. Is this customer-impacting?

customer-success-alex: several active customers reported slow streaming responses (1 customer filed a support ticket), not a hard outage but UX broken. Happening across hosted-prod clusters in us-west-2 only.

jit: pulling KV node logs. we see prefill request queue long, but decode workers idle for some queues. prefill traffic to KV increased by ~3x from a handful of long prompts. evidence of prefill vs decode imbalance (prefill heavy, decode under-pressure due to slab fragmentation).

mike: can you paste the hot log snippets?

jit: sure:

```
2026-03-15T10:41:52Z kv-node-17 INFO eviction: slab_shrink triggered slab_id=3 freed=2MB total_slab=512MB
2026-03-15T10:41:53Z kv-node-17 WARN prefill_queue_len=187 decode_queue_len=22 prefill_rate=120/s decode_rate=8/s
2026-03-15T10:42:10Z kv-node-17 INFO eviction: aggressive_run items_evicted=143
```

sara: that log line matches fragmentation: small allocations causing many tiny holes, GC scheduling reacting by freeing slabs -> high eviction churn. When eviction occurs, prefetches miss and streaming waits on network+disk, amplifies p99.

ashley: initial mitigation ideas: 1) increase slab retention limit to avoid immediate shrink (temp), 2) throttle prefill path per-tenant to even decode/prefill ratio, 3) route streaming to model-fallback that is less KV-intensive. Which can we do fastest?

mike: order of operations: low-risk first. 1) set slab_retention to 30s (was 5s) on affected pool-kv-17 (hot patch), 2) apply per-tenant prefill throttle for top 5 tenants to reduce prefill spikes, 3) prepare fallback routing for streaming to crackpipe-small-01 if needed.

ops-robin: doing slab_retention change now via remote flags. command:

```
kubectl -n infra exec kv-node-17 -- /bin/kvctl set-flag slab_retention=30
```

ops-robin: flag applied to pool-kv-17. monitoring.

deploy-bot: rollout detected: infra/kv-node config patch slab_retention=30 on pool-kv-17 by ops-robin at 2026-03-15T10:44:12Z.

mike: check metrics after 1m.

(1m later)

ashley: eviction/sec dropped from x5 to x1.4, prefill_queue_len down to ~50. p99 decreased: 1.25s -> 420ms. p95 improved to ~180ms. still above SLO for some tenants.

jit: decode workers still underutilized in shard-2; fragmentation remains but improved. recommend throttling prefill for top noisy tenants for 10m window.

mike: @ops-robin please apply per-tenant token throttle for tenants t-42, t-91, t-13: set prefill_max_inflight=8. Command: 

```
kv-ops apply-tenant-config --pool pool-kv-17 --tenant t-42 --prefill-max-inflight 8
```

ops-robin: applied to t-42,t-91,t-13.

ashley: seeing immediate reduction in prefill_rate for those tenants. overall p99 ~ 310ms. still some streaming stalls at tail; suspect residual slab worn fragmentation + occasional eviction cycles triggered by background compaction.

mike: good. next low-lift: enable decode-worker backpressure so decode_pool pulls tasks from prefill only when decode_queue_len < 60. Can we toggle at runtime?

jit: yes, can enable backpressure gate. Doing it for pool-kv-17 now.

```
kvctl set-flag decode_backpressure_threshold=60 --pool pool-kv-17
```

jit: enabled.

(2m later)

ashley: decode utilization normalized. p99 now ~230ms, p95 ~150ms. error rate back to baseline. streaming stalls rare.

mike: good progress. Customer-impact: CS reported one major customer with degraded streaming — notified them of mitigation.

customer-success-alex: customer notified, they confirmed improved behaviour, asked for RCA and ETA for permanent fix.

mike: immediate actions we took: slab_retention bump, tenant prefill throttle, decode backpressure. Short-term status: stabilized, p99 down <300ms.

sara: longer-term follow-ups (action items): 1) investigate slab allocation pattern and increase slab size for pool-kv-17, 2) add autoscaling rules to increase decode workers on sustained prefill bursts, 3) surface per-tenant prefill ratios in console, 4) better eviction-green zones to avoid compaction during peak streaming.

ashley: logging: file a SEV review if customer complains further. For now mark incident as mitigated and hand off to daytime oncall.

mike: handing off to daytime oncall @sara. notes: mitigation applied, watch p99/p95 for next 2 hours, rollback slab_retention back to 5s only after confirming no re-fragmentation for 1h.

sara: acked. I'll own the follow-ups and open a tracking ticket.

deploy-bot: incident mitigation changelog appended to incident-5601234567: slab_retention=30 (kv-node-17), tenant throttles applied (t-42,t-91,t-13), decode_backpressure_threshold=60.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated - 2026-03-15T10:48Z. P95/P99 trending down. Handoff to daytime oncall.

mike: closing from my side. if anything reappears ping this thread and I'll re-open. :thumbsup:
